Terraform main.tf:54-61,96-104 grants Workers R2 Storage Write+Read on the bucket in one token, and no lock or versioning resource exists. docs/backups-cloud-runbook.md:11-17 itself says the live bucket recycle-db-backup is unmanaged and 'one credential both uploads and deletes ... no object lock or versioning'. describe-service pg-r2-backup lists R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID/R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as Railway variables, which the 2026-10-21 Railway env-var breach exposed. The owner's 2026-10-23 rotation record still lists 'R2 x3' as pending.
verdicts.reason: The design defect is verified directly. Two parts are not verified: whether the R2 keys have been rotated since 2026-10-23 (values and ages can't be read under the ground rules), and whether the live bucket has a bucket lock (wrangler isn't installed here, and pnpm install is forbidden). Both go to needs_owner. P1 is right, because a leaked key that can read and delete every full prod dump threatens both confidentiality and recoverability.

verdicts.evidence: describe-service backend: production source {branch: main, checkSuites: false}; dev source {branch: dev, checkSuites: false}. 'gh api repos/JinhuW/recycle_servres_erp/branches/{main,dev}/protection' returns enforce_admins/allow_deletions but no required_status_checks key, so no check is required. apps/backend/Dockerfile:68 CMD runs 'node ./scripts/migrate.mjs' before start, so a deploy applies migrations to prod at boot.
verdicts.reason: Railway doesn't wait for GitHub checks, and GitHub doesn't require them before a merge, so a red main merge builds and migrates prod. In practice the normal flow (feature PR CI, then dev, then release) reduces the risk, so P2 is right, not P1.

It builds fleet_proxies from 0213 on a disposable PG18, inserts one row, and runs scrub.sql's DO block: 'ERROR: null value in column "url_enc" of relation "fleet_proxies" violates not-null constraint', psql rc=3. Live: db-sync dev logs show the same error at 2026-10-28T04:04, 10-29T04:03, 10-30T04:01 and 10-31T04:02, while deployment 5fecc5a6 stays SUCCESS. sync.sh:111-116 runs everything in one --single-transaction with ON_ERROR_STOP, so the whole restore rolls back, leaving dev at the last good copy, and sync.sh has no alert path.
verdicts.reason: Every nightly sync since 2026-10-28 rolls back, and nothing is visible outside the logs. tests/sync-scrub.test.ts never inserts a fleet_proxies row, so CI misses it. P2 is right: dev and QA data go stale, prod is unaffected.

verdicts.evidence: describe-service backend: production watchPatterns=[apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**]; dev watchPatterns=[apps/backend/**, packages/shared/**, package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml, tsconfig.base.json]. Neither list includes pnpm-workspace.yaml, which holds overrides at lines 15-21.
verdicts.reason: The config drift is real, but its reach is narrow, so it drops to P3. A dev->main release merge almost always also touches apps/backend/**, and that rebuild takes the new lockfile with it. Only a release made of nothing but lockfile or manifest changes is skipped. An override change in pnpm-workspace.yaml also rewrites pnpm-lock.yaml, so the 'neither watches pnpm-workspace.yaml' part matters only for build-flag edits like allowBuilds. The fix is still cheap: copy dev's patterns to prod.
